summary_one_line: A blind plaintiff (represented by Carlson Lynch) sued HCA Holdings in 2017 over 159 hospital websites lacking alt-text and keyboard navigation, making them inaccessible to screen reader users — the case established healthcare as a high-risk sector.
notes: Filed January 25, 2017. Plaintiffs' firm: Carlson Lynch. The case alleged that websites of more than 100 hospitals and healthcare facilities owned by HCA 'are not accessible to blind individuals and therefore violate Title III of the Americans with Disabilities Act.' Specific barrier: websites 'do not inter-operate well with assistive technology used by disabled persons such as screen readers.' Outcome/docket not confirmed — status unknown after initial filings. Marked verified: false for docket and outcome. HCA is now HCA Healthcare, operating 180+ hospitals and 2,300+ sites of care. Included as historical precedent establishing healthcare sector vulnerability.
